ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are three horizontal straight lines that are mutually parallel, labeled l1, l2, l3; two oblique lines a and b respectively intersect these three parallel lines. The intersection points of oblique line a with l1, l2, l3 are A, B, C in order, so AB is the intercepted segment between l1 and l2, and BC is the intercepted segment between l2 and l3. The intersection points of oblique line b with l1, l2, l3 are D, E, F in order, so DE corresponds to AB, and EF corresponds to BC. Then reason: because l1 ∥ l2 ∥ l3, according to the theorem that parallel lines divide line segments proportionally, there is AB/BC = DE/EF. It is known that AB:BC = 1:2, so DE:EF = 1:2. Also DE = 2, therefore EF = 2 × 2 = 4.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it shows three parallel horizontal lines labeled l1, l2, l3 cut by two slanted transversals a and b. On transversal a, the intersections with l1, l2, l3 are A, B, C, so AB is the segment between l1 and l2 and BC is between l2 and l3. On transversal b, the corresponding segments are DE and EF. Read from the text that l1 ∥ l2 ∥ l3, AB:BC = 1:2, and DE = 2. Apply the intercept theorem for several parallel lines cut by two transversals: corresponding intercepted segments are proportional, so AB/BC = DE/EF = 1/2. Solve 2/EF = 1/2 to get EF = 4.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the three lines l1, l2, l3 are parallel, and the slanted line a meets them at A, B, C while slanted line b meets them at D, E, F. Treat the parallel lines as horizontal levels. Along any fixed slanted transversal, the length of the segment between two parallel levels is proportional to the perpendicular spacing between those two levels. From the text, AB:BC = 1:2, so the spacing between l1 and l2 is half the spacing between l2 and l3. The same two spacings determine DE and EF on transversal b, so DE:EF = 1:2. Since DE = 2, EF must be twice as long, giving EF = 4.
